stories.head: SpaceX secures $1.6 billion in military launches
stories.body: SpaceX has clinched $1.6 billion in military satellite launch orders, reinforcing its dominance in the defense sector. This latest win underscores the military's ongoing reliance on Falcon 9, which remains the go-to rocket for many high-stakes missions. With the U.S. military increasingly outsourcing launch capabilities, SpaceX seems to be the only game in town.
stories.soWhat: The military's love affair with SpaceX suggests that competitors may need to rethink their strategies, as loyalty often trumps innovation in government contracts.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190 million for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly has raised $190 million in a Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The company focuses on co-orbital security and space domain awareness, illustrating that in the current landscape, cash can often outweigh actual innovation. With defense contracts on the horizon, True Anomaly is positioning itself as a critical player in a rapidly evolving sector.
stories.soWhat: This funding round highlights a growing trend where investors prioritize defense capabilities, even if the technology isn't yet fully developed.

stories.head: Sophia Space and Caltech patent space data centers
stories.body: Sophia Space and Caltech have patented a modular design for space-based data centers, aiming to capitalize on the increasing demand for data storage in orbit. This patent could lead to new business models in the space data sector, as companies look to leverage low-latency access to data. The vacuum of space might just be the next frontier for data management.
stories.soWhat: As traditional data centers face capacity issues, this patent could signal a shift in how we think about data storage—if you're not in space, are you even in the game?

watchlist.title: L3Harris IPO delay impacts market sentiment
watchlist.body: With L3Harris pushing its missile business IPO to 2027, investors may become wary of the defense sector's immediate prospects.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris tactical bid heats up
watchlist.body: The collaboration for a tactical SDA constellation bid could set the stage for a new wave of competitive bidding in military contracts.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's next moves post-funding
watchlist.body: Investors will be watching closely to see how True Anomaly deploys its new capital to secure government contracts.

watchlist.title: SpaceX's military orders may draw scrutiny
watchlist.body: As SpaceX continues to dominate military launches, regulatory bodies may start looking closer at potential monopolistic practices.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
